main_text.l: AD CLARISSIMVM VIRVM IACOBVM LECTIVM Iurisconsultum, cùm ad illum superiores versus legendos misisset.

l.i: CVr tibi quem primos inter numeramus amicos Carmina postremo nostra legenda damus? Consultum Iuris ne lite moremur iniqua, Lecti, peccatum rusticitate vides.

SErus vbi solidam reddit cum fœnore sortem Debitor, ista mihi non male grata mora est: Atqui non sortem, non vllum fœnus amico Debueras vltro pendis vtrunque tamen. Illa voco sortem maiore sonanda cothurno. Fœnus versiculi sunt mihi nempe tui.

page.notes: The title line reads "AD CLARISSIMVM VIRVM IACOBVM LECTIVM" in capitals with a second line in small capitals; the poem's initial letters C and S are large woodcut initials, transcribed with their following words. The verse uses long s as plain s. Ornaments are not text.
